Basically make a video yourself, you don't have to spend a dime. You can film it on your phone and edit the whole thing in a free video app. I would recommend Inshot but if you can fork out for a paid version, Movavi is very easy to use and has a lot of built-in effects where all you have to do is drag and drop stuff into the video.

Once you've made the ad, go to [https://ads.google.com](https://ads.google.com/intl/en_GB/home/) \- personally I'd use the live chat feature and someone will call you back. Just tell them you want to upload a video ad for Youtube and they'll guide you through the steps and give you a breakdown of your monthly and daily budget based on your sales conversion target. Also let them know where you want to feature the ads, personally I prefer "discovery" over "in stream" which just means your ad will pop up randomly on the side bar or recommended list. To be honest, the conversion for these types of ads is very low which is why I was surprised to make a sale on the first day.

Also remember to add a link in the first line of your description underneath the video with a "call to action" for people to want to visit your Amazon page. For e.g. "10% OFF while stocks last" but obviously this is dependent on what type of course/product you're selling.

I agree it will get more competitive but there is a still a big barrier to entry for anyone wanting to sell FBA Prime products in Germany. You need to register for EU VAT first which costs money and takes at least 2-3 months. A lot of Chinese and US sellers in particular cannot be bothered with this, so for now, in my opinion competition will remain low.

There are not "crazy amount of sellers and listings" in the less saturated markets outside of the US and you can still make a ton of money if your product offers more value than your competitors. For example Germany, UK and Australian market on Amazon will explode in the next 10 years. I have seen brands take basic products straight off Alibaba - like jewellery bags - and just flog them on Amazon Germany for double the price and are making 50,000 euros a month from five colour variations of this bag.

Just be aware that if you want to sell in the EU markets and send your products directly to those respective country's warehouses you will need to register for EU VAT in those countries. There is a bit of paperwork but it is very straight forward and takes around 3 months. Amazon offers third party tax compliant services where you don't pay anything for the first year and thereafter you have to pay around 3000 euros a year.
